Show the mutable default argument trap.

Supplied answer
def wrong(item, box=[]): # BAD: the list is created only once
    box.append(item)
    return box
print(wrong(1)) # [1]
print(wrong(2)) # [1, 2] -> surprise!
def right(item, box=None): # GOOD
    if box is None:
        box = []
    box.append(item)
    return box
print(right(1), right(2)) # [1] [2]
Note: Never use a list or dict as a default value. Use None and create it inside.
